relationship: André worked on the same team as Marcos (peers)
text:
I worked alongside Marcos for four years at House Numbers, from a handful of services to a sixteen-service platform, from a B2C web-app into a B2B dashboard. We were peers the whole way.

Most engineers claiming AI-agent experience arrived in the last 2 years, with the boom of ChatGPT and similar tools. Marcos did not. In 2022, he built our mortgage eligibility and pricing engine: a declarative matcher framework scoring HECM, HELOC and HELOAN products, with parallel eligibility checks and product definitions validated by types rather than convention. In 2023, he built our conversational service: stateful intents that adapted to what we already knew about a user, persisted chat history, and retro-filling of context when data arrived late. So when LLM agents came, he already knew what an automated decision system has to survive before people will trust it.

Marcos went straight for the unglamorous parts when needed. He was the one who designed our LLM-as-a-judge scorers, an *.agents.ts convention that isolates model-dependent code in a CI lane that only fires when a prompt or an agent actually changes, making sure our test suite would be reliable even thought LLMs are not deterministic and that we would not run real-model evals on every pull request. He was the one who defended that "OpenAI grading OpenAI's own output" tends to have a bias, and he moved our model selection out of environment variables so we could judge with an opposing provider.

Most recent, his document-extraction proof of concept beat our incumbent vendor's field-reading accuracy at roughly $0.30 per loan against their $25. He also replaced 24 hand-written MCP tool files with a declarative factory that tripled our agent's tool coverage. He became the person all of us pinged about email triage and communications in our product, without ever claiming ownership of it, just because we trust his analysis skills and overall knowledge of the product and its flows. And, to put a cherry on top, Marcos built his own tooling, including his own agent CLI, being a champion of AI tooling in our team, always sharing and teaching our team.

Marcos (or Paco, as we kindly call him) is a great asset to any team, and a even greater friend. He is kind, communicative, proactive, and a great team player. Marcos was an essential part of the culture we built at House Numbers, and a crucial part of the product we built. I would recommend him a thousand times!
